# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

import subprocess, os, pathlib, shutil, re
def run(args,cwd="/tmp/t"):
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args,cwd=cwd,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=15)
    return r.stdout,r.stderr,r.returncode
def prep(files):
    p=pathlib.Path("/tmp/t")
    if p.exists(): shutil.rmtree(p)
    p.mkdir(parents=True)
    for k,v in files.items():
        (p/k).parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True); (p/k).write_text(v)
def chap(content_md="# MyChap\nHi para\n## Sub\nMore\n"):
    if os.path.exists("/tmp/t/o.html"):
        txt=open("/tmp/t/o.html").read()
        m=re.search(r'class = "chapter">(.*)',txt,re.S)
        return repr(m.group(1)[:800]) if m else txt[-800:]
    return None

prefixes=["+","-","++","--","+++","---","!","!!","+ +","- -","+-","-+","+", "#","*","0","1"," "]
for pre in prefixes:
    prep({"doc.md":"# MyChap\nHi para\n## Sub\nMore\n","b.book":f"title: T\noutput.html: o.html\n{pre} doc.md\n"})
    o,e,c=run(["-n","b.book"])
    print(f"pre={pre!r} err={e.strip()!r} chap={chap()}")
    print()
PY

import subprocess, os, pathlib, shutil
def run(args,cwd,inp=None):
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args,cwd=cwd,capture_output=True,text=True,input=inp,timeout=20)
    return r.stdout,r.stderr,r.returncode
def prep(files,dir="/tmp/t"):
    p=pathlib.Path(dir)
    if p.exists(): shutil.rmtree(p)
    p.mkdir(parents=True)
    for k,v in files.items():
        fp=p/k; fp.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True); fp.write_text(v) if isinstance(v,str) else fp.write_bytes(v)

# asset test.book scenario
prep({"test.md":"# Chapitre\n\nBonjour ! Comment ça va ? « Test » : voilà ; oui.\n","test.book":open("/workspace/assets/test.book").read()},"/tmp/asset")

for f in os.listdir("/tmp/asset"):
    print(f, os.path.getsize(f"/tmp/asset/{f}"))

# odt via config
prep({"doc.md":"# C\nHi\n","b.book":"title: T\noutput.odt: o.odt\n+ doc.md\n"})
o,e,c=run(["-n","b.book"],"/tmp/t"); print("odt config",repr(e),os.listdir("/tmp/t"))
# output list
prep({"doc.md":"# C\nHi\n","b.book":"title: T\noutput: [html, epub, tex]\n+ doc.md\n"})
o,e,c=run(["-n","b.book"],"/tmp/t"); print("output list",repr(e),os.listdir("/tmp/t"))
# output with other syntax?
prep({"doc.md":"# C\nHi\n","b.book":"title: T\noutput: [html]\n+ doc.md\n"})
o,e,c=run(["-n","b.book"],"/tmp/t"); print("output [html]",repr(e),os.listdir("/tmp/t"))
# no output specified
prep({"doc.md":"# C\nHi\n","b.book":"title: T\n+ doc.md\n"})
o,e,c=run(["-n","b.book"],"/tmp/t"); print("no output",repr(e),os.listdir("/tmp/t"))
PY"}

import subprocess, pathlib, shutil, os
def prep():
    p=pathlib.Path("/tmp/t2")
    if p.exists(): shutil.rmtree(p)
    p.mkdir(parents=True)
    (p/"a.md").write_text("# A\nHi\n"); (p/"c.md").write_text("# C\nHo\n")
def run(args):
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args,cwd="/tmp/t2",capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
    return r.stdout,r.stderr,r.returncode

trials=[
 ["-c","a.md"],
 ["new.book","-c","a.md"],
 ["-c","a.md","new.book"], # greedy?
 ["new.book","-c","a.md","c.md"],
 ["-S","new.book","-c","a.md"],
 ["new.book","--create","a.md"],
 ["-o","new.book","-t","html","-c","a.md"],
]
for a in trials:
    prep(); o,e,c=run(a)
    print(a,repr(e),repr(o[:200]),sorted(os.listdir("/tmp/t2")))
    if os.path.exists("/tmp/t2/new.book"):
        print(" new.book content:",repr(open("/tmp/t2/new.book").read()))

# create when file exists
prep(); pathlib.Path("/tmp/t2/new.book").write_text("old")
o,e,c=run(["new.book","-c","a.md"]); print("exists",repr(e),repr(o),open("/tmp/t2/new.book").read())
# create - stdout exact bytes
prep(); o,e,c=run(["-c","a.md","c.md"]); print("create stdout exact",repr(o))

import subprocess, pathlib, shutil, os, re
def book(chapters, files, cfg_extra=""):
    p=pathlib.Path("/tmp/t")
    if p.exists(): shutil.rmtree(p)
    p.mkdir()
    for k,v in files.items(): (p/k).write_text(v)
    (p/"b.book").write_text("title: T\noutput.html: o.html\noutput.tex: o.tex\n"+cfg_extra+chapters)
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-n","b.book"],cwd=p,capture_output=True,text=True)
    html=open(p/"o.html").read() if os.path.exists(p/"o.html") else ""
    tex=open(p/"o.tex").read() if os.path.exists(p/"o.tex") else ""
    # extract toc/nav and chapters
    nav=html[html.find("<nav"):html.find("</nav>")] if "<nav" in html else ""

import re

NBSP='\u00a0'; NNBSP='\u202f'; ENSP='\u2002'

def smart_quotes(s):
    # Double quotes state
    res=[]; in_d=False
    # First process double quotes by scanning and building list, while leaving singles for later? Need interaction: single quote pair determination based original string maybe independent.
    chars=list(s)
    # Double
    i=0; out=[]
    for idx,ch in enumerate(chars):
        if ch!='"':
            out.append(ch); continue
        prev=chars[idx-1] if idx>0 else ''
        nxt=chars[idx+1] if idx+1 < len(chars) else ''
        if not in_d:
            can_open = (nxt!='' and not nxt.isspace()) and (prev=='' or prev.isspace() or prev in '([{<—–-/"\'“‘«')
            if can_open:
                out.append('“'); in_d=True
            else:
                out.append('"')
        else:
            can_close = (prev!='' and not prev.isspace()) and (nxt=='' or nxt.isspace() or nxt in '.,;:!?%)]}’”')
            if can_close:
                out.append('”'); in_d=False
            else:
                out.append('"')
    s=''.join(out)
    # Single quotes
    chars=list(s); out=[]; in_s=False
    def has_closing(pos):
        # find later ' that could close: preceded nonspace, followed end/space/punct
        for j in range(pos+1,len(chars)):
            if chars[j]=="'":
                prev=chars[j-1] if j>0 else ''
                nxt=chars[j+1] if j+1 < len(chars) else ''
                if prev and not prev.isspace() and (nxt=='' or nxt.isspace() or nxt in '.,;:!?%)]}”’'):
                    return True
        return False
    for idx,ch in enumerate(chars):
        if ch!="'":
            out.append(ch); continue
        prev=chars[idx-1] if idx>0 else ''
        nxt=chars[idx+1] if idx+1 < len(chars) else ''
        if in_s:
            can_close=(prev!='' and not prev.isspace()) and (nxt=='' or nxt.isspace() or nxt in '.,;:!?%)]}”')
            if can_close:
                out.append('’'); in_s=False
            else:
                # apostrophe inside? e.g. 'a 'b' c' second opening-like became ’ in reference; treat as ’ if between nonspace/start and letter
                out.append('’')
            continue
        # not in single quote
        # Apostrophe between letters/digits, or after letter before space/end (possessive), or before letter at start if no closing pair
        can_open=(nxt!='' and not nxt.isspace()) and (prev=='' or prev.isspace() or prev in '([{<—–-/"“«') and has_closing(idx)
        if can_open:
            out.append('‘'); in_s=True
        else:
            # If isolated between spaces or alone, leave straight
            if (prev=='' or prev.isspace()) and (nxt=='' or nxt.isspace()):
                out.append("'")
            elif prev=='' and nxt=='':
                out.append("'")
            else:
                # apostrophe
                # But if prev is space and next is space already handled. If prev start and next letter with no closing => ’ (elision)
                out.append('’')
    return ''.join(out)

def clean_french(s):
    # Ellipsis
    s=s.replace('...','…')
    # Guillemets pairs and unpaired
    s=_clean_guillemets(s)
    # Dashes (em/en) spacing after/before
    s=_clean_dashes(s)
    # Punctuation ! ? ; % and :
    # % only after digit
    s=re.sub(r'([0-9])[ ]+%',r'\1'+NNBSP+'%',s)
    # sequence of !? etc: replace spaces before one of !?; chars, if preceding is not space/start and punctuation not part of something? Use regex.
    # To avoid semicolon etc in URLs no spaces anyway.
    s=re.sub(r'([^\s])[ ]+([!?;])',lambda m: m.group(1)+NNBSP+m.group(2),s)
    s=re.sub(r'([^\s])[ ]+(:)',lambda m: m.group(1)+NBSP+m.group(2),s)
    return s

def _clean_guillemets(s):
    # Process pairs stack
    out=[]; i=0
    # We'll scan and when encountering «, look for a later » in same string.
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i]=='«':
            # determine if preceded by space in already output/current s and there is nonspace before that
            prev_char=s[i-1] if i>0 else ''
            desired=NBSP
            close=s.find('»',i+1)
            if close!=-1 and prev_char==' ':
                # if there's a nonspace character before prev space
                # look backwards
                k=i-2
                has=False
                while k>=0:
                    if not s[k].isspace(): has=True; break
                    k-=1
                if has:
                    desired=NNBSP
            out.append('«')
            # consume spaces after
            j=i+1
            has_space=False
            while j < len(s) and s[j]==' ':
                has_space=True; j+=1
            if has_space:
                out.append(desired)
            if close!=-1:
                # process content up to close, but punctuation inside will be processed later by caller? Our events order: guillemets before punctuation, content spaces before ! remain.
                # Copy content except trailing spaces converted before close
                content=s[j:close]
                # split trailing spaces
                stripped=content.rstrip(' ')
                trailing=len(content)-len(stripped)
                out.append(stripped)
                if trailing>0:
                    out.append(desired)
                out.append('»')
                i=close+1
                continue
            else:
                i=j; continue
        elif s[i]=='»':
            # unpaired closing: spaces before it in out text? Our out may already have spaces appended char by char. Replace trailing spaces in out.
            # Remove trailing spaces from out and add NBSP if there were
            text=''.join(out)
            stripped=text.rstrip(' ')
            if len(text)!=len(stripped):
                out=[stripped, NBSP, '»']
            else:
                out.append('»')
            i+=1; continue
        else:
            out.append(s[i]); i+=1
    return ''.join(out)

def _clean_dashes(s):
    # Pair handling for em dash and en dash separately within this string
    # We'll operate on list chars and make replacements of spaces adjacent.
    # Find positions of dash chars that have a following space and non? 
    # Determine pair toggle by all dash chars (—/– mixed?) Use em only toggle; en likely same (?) treat individually.
    chars=list(s)
    # indices of em dashes that are surrounded / followed
    # Count dashes with a space after (potential incidence). If at least 2, first is opening, second closing alternating.
    dash_positions=[idx for idx,c in enumerate(chars) if c in ('—','–')]
    # only consider those with following regular space for pairing? un — deux — pair both have spaces. a—b doesn't.
    candidate=[idx for idx in dash_positions if idx+1 < len(chars) and chars[idx+1]==' ']
    # But closing dash in pair is also candidate. Pair them sequentially.
    closing=set()
    if len(candidate)>=2:
        # If there are exactly 2 candidates or pairs, mark every second as closing.
        # Heuristic: pair up candidates (0,1), (2,3)...
        for k in range(1,len(candidate),2):
            closing.add(candidate[k])
    # Build output with replacement decisions, taking spacing before closing into account without messing indices: iterate original.
    out=[]; i=0
    while i < len(chars):
        c=chars[i]
        if c in ('—','–'):
            if i in closing:
                # Replace trailing spaces in out with NBSP if present, output dash, then following spaces as one regular space (consume them)
                text=''.join(out); stripped=text.rstrip(' ')
                if len(text)!=len(stripped):
                    out=[stripped, NBSP]
                out.append(c)
                # consume spaces after and output a single regular space if there were and not end
                j=i+1; has=False
                while j < len(chars) and chars[j]==' ':
                    has=True; j+=1
                if has and j < len(chars):
                    out.append(' ')
                elif has:
                    # trailing spaces at end will be trimmed by renderer? keep none? Original 'a — ' para becomes 'a —' because trailing whitespace in source para is stripped by markdown? Our earlier output had no trailing.
                    pass
                i=j; continue
            else:
                out.append(c)
                j=i+1; has=False
                while j < len(chars) and chars[j]==' ':
                    has=True; j+=1
                if has and j < len(chars):
                    # if preceded by space (original char before dash is space) -> NBSP else ENSP
                    prev=chars[i-1] if i>0 else ''
                    if prev==' ':
                        out.append(NBSP)
                    else:
                        out.append(ENSP)
                i=j if has else i+1
                continue
        out.append(c); i+=1
    return ''.join(out)

def clean_text(s, options, book_lang='en'):
    # options is Options instance or dict-like getter
    def get(k,default=None):
        try: return options.get(k,default) 
        except Exception: return default
    if not get('input.clean',True):
        return s
    # Ligatures first? If dashes ligature converts, french cleaning will adjust spaces after.
    if get('input.clean.ligature.dashes',False):
        s=s.replace('---','—').replace('--','–')
    if get('input.clean.ligature.guillemets',False):
        s=s.replace('<<','«').replace('>>','»')
    # French-specific
    lang=str(book_lang or 'en')
    if lang.startswith('fr'):
        s=clean_french(s)
    if get('input.clean.smart_quotes',True):
        s=smart_quotes(s)

        # deprecated alias
        orig_key=key_str
        if key_str=='output.html_dir':
            LOG.warn("'output.html_dir' has been deprecated, you should now use 'output.html.dir'")
            key_str='output.html.dir'
        if key_str not in SPECS:
            return f"unrecognized key '{key_str}'"
        if only_if_absent and key_str in self.present:
            # still need type validation? Reference imported options that are already present: are errors still logged?
            # Likely options are only added if absent after conversion; conversion errors from imported file were logged during its own load.
            return None
        typ,rawdef=SPECS[key_str]
        target_values=self.cli if layer=='cli' else self.values
        target_present=self.cli_present if layer=='cli' else self.present
        # Import is handled by caller in many cases, but store it too; type path
        # Conversion
        if typ in ('metadata','string','path','template path'):
            if not isinstance(yval,Y) or yval.tag!='String':
                return f"Expected a string as value for key {key_str}, found {yaml_debug(yval)}"
            target_values[key_str]=yval.value; target_present.add(key_str); 
            if source: self.opt_source[key_str]=source
            return None
        if typ=='boolean':
            if not isinstance(yval,Y) or yval.tag!='Boolean':
                return f"expected a boolean as value for key '{key_str}', found {yaml_debug(yval)}"
            target_values[key_str]=bool(yval.value); target_present.add(key_str)
            if source: self.opt_source[key_str]=source
            return None
        if typ=='integer':
            if not isinstance(yval,Y) or yval.tag!='Integer':
                return f"expected an integer as value for key '{key_str}', found {yaml_debug(yval)}"
            target_values[key_str]=int(yval.value); target_present.add(key_str)
            if source: self.opt_source[key_str]=source
            return None
        if typ=='list of strings':
            if not isinstance(yval,Y) or yval.tag!='Array':
                return f"Expected a list as value for key {key_str}, found {yaml_debug(yval)}"
            # validate all strings first? Reference for resources.files reported first non-string and presumably doesn't set.
            vals=[]
            for elem in yval.value:
                if elem.tag!='String':
                    # For output, processing is sequential and earlier formats may have taken effect - handled below before this check?
                    if key_str=='output':
                        # will have been handled sequentially; but we are here generic.
                        pass
                    return f"Expected only strings in the list for key {key_str}, found {yaml_debug(elem)}"
                vals.append(elem.value)
            if key_str=='output':
                # sequential
                for fmt in vals:
                    f=fmt
                    if f=='html_dir':
                        LOG.warn("'output.html_dir' has been deprecated, you should now use 'output.html.dir'")
                        f='html.dir'
                    if f not in FORMAT_KEYS:
                        return f"The output format {fmt} for key output is not recognized"
                    dest_key=FORMAT_KEYS[f]
                    # set to "auto" sentinel
                    target_values[dest_key]='auto'; target_present.add(dest_key)
                    if source: self.opt_source[dest_key]=source
                # output itself not present? Might mark present but not needed
                target_values[key_str]=vals; target_present.add(key_str)
                return None
            else:
                target_values[key_str]=vals; target_present.add(key_str)
                if source: self.opt_source[key_str]=source
                return None
        # fallback string
        if not isinstance(yval,Y) or yval.tag!='String':
            return f"Expected a string as value for key {key_str}, found {yaml_debug(yval)}"
        target_values[key_str]=yval.value; target_present.add(key_str); return None
    def set_from_string(self,key_str,value_str,only_if_absent=False,source=None,layer='normal'):
        # --set values are parsed as a single YAML value

def build_toc(book):
    roots=[]; stack=[]
    num_depth=book.options.get_int('rendering.num_depth',1)
    def add(node):
        # stack contains nodes with level < node.level that are ancestors
        while stack and stack[-1].level>=node.level:
            stack.pop()
        if stack:
            stack[-1].children.append(node)
        else:
            roots.append(node)
        stack.append(node)
    for idx,elem in enumerate(book.elements):
        if elem.kind=='part':
            title_inlines=elem.title_inlines if elem.title_inlines is not None else []
            node=TocNode(title_inlines,getattr(elem,'plain_title',''),getattr(elem,'link_id',0),0,True,getattr(elem,'number_str',None),True,idx)
            add(node)
        elif elem.kind=='file':
            for b in elem.blocks:
                if b.kind!='heading': continue
                if b.level>num_depth: continue
                node=TocNode(b.children,getattr(b,'plain_title',''),getattr(b,'link_id',0),b.level,bool(getattr(b,'numbered',False)),getattr(b,'number_str',None),False,idx)
                add(node)
    return roots
